reviews.author: MY
reviews.text:
On December 23, 2025, around 7:30 p.m., I visited the store to use a Hana Card discount coupon.
From the beginning, a person (I don't know if he was the owner or part-time worker) who looked like an old lady with a bad impression and was unfriendly responded.

1. Garbage bag payment related
When I paid for a garbage bag (2,500 won) and asked if I could earn points, I was told, “I can’t because there is a discount.”
After paying, I came out and checked, and found that the payment was made without the 2,000 won discount applied, so I went back in to get a receipt.
I asked for a refund because I was told that the discount does not apply to garbage bags.
He said condescendingly, “We don’t normally accept credit card payments for trash bags, but I did it for you.”

Then shouldn't they have informed you that you couldn't pay from the first time you tried to pay?
Also, I wonder if they could have explained it to me in advance if they had known that the discount had not been applied when making the payment.

2. Problem with wine payment and discount voucher information
When I tried to pay for the wine after receiving the refund, he suddenly got annoyed and said that the discount coupon does not apply to alcohol.
I even heard sarcasm like, “Are you from another planet?”

However, at the bottom of the discount coupon it was clearly stated that alcohol was applicable, and the discount was actually applied at the time of payment.
I asked if I could earn points after the discount.
I heard the answer, “You should have accumulated points before applying the discount!”

How does the customer know about the system?
Isn’t this something the staff should first inform you about before making payment?

From the first impression, I felt the lack of humanity and unfriendliness throughout the entire service, so this is a store I don't want to visit again.
I don't know if it's the owner or the employee, but I hope you think again about customer service.
I was so angry that I had to leave a review. I hope others will reconsider when visiting.

reviews.author: Son Hoyoung
reviews.text: I went to Mokmyeoksanbang on Namsan Dulle-gil. It is a recognized restaurant that is also listed by Michelin and introduced in the Wednesday Gourmet Bibimbap section. Meals taste even better when eaten in an old-fashioned and beautiful hanok. Bibimbap costs less than 10,000 won, so it is very cost-effective. When I asked for more bean sprout soup, they kindly refilled it for me. You can also eat more young radish kimchi, which is crunchy and delicious. The poached chicken, egg and soy sauce bibimbap was delicious because it was seasoned well, and the hand tofu ssambap was also very good with the combination of stir-fried kimchi and tofu. I also recommend the cheese kimchi pancake as it is savory and spicy. This is a place I want to visit when I have a meal with foreign friends. I think they would be very happy if we served the traditional food, bibimbap, in a traditional house called Hanok. It's nice inside and there's seating outside as well. When the weather gets warm, it might be nice to eat outside. I also received medicine through a Naver review event and ate it. It was a very enjoyable day as I was able to take a walk around Namsan Mountain after eating.

reviews.author: Majimata
reviews.text:
Seoul Namsan Tower (official name: N Seoul Tower) is a representative landmark located at the top of Namsan Mountain in the center of Seoul. It is built on Namsan Mountain, approximately 236 meters above sea level, and is a famous attraction that offers a panoramic view of Seoul.

Namsan Tower is divided into ‘Seoul Tower Plaza’ from the 1st to 4th floors and ‘N Seoul Tower’ from the 5th floor to the observatory.
From the 1st to 4th floors, there is a gallery, lounge, game plaza, media art, and various stores, and on the 5th floor, there is a path to the observatory, an information desk, N gift shop, and a cafe. The T1 to T7 floors after the 5th floor are composed of various facilities such as an observatory, restaurants, and cafes.
The buildings around Namsan Tower also have restaurants, convenience stores, and event zones.

From the observatory at the top of the tower, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the city during the day and a gorgeous night view at night. The ‘love locks’, which are locks attached to the railing of the building below the tower, are also famous, making it a popular date spot for couples.
In addition, there are various observatories around the summit, so even if you do not climb the tower, you can enjoy the view comfortably from various places, and various events and light shows are also held.

There are various routes to climb Namsan Mountain to N Seoul Tower, but the most recommended route is through Baekbeom Square on the west (the entrance is also the nicest). It passes through a wonderful square with traces of an old fortress, and there are attractions such as the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall and the Hanyangdoseong Relics Exhibition Hall. The wide, well-groomed mountain path has a gentle slope, so you can enjoy the scenery comfortably. (The climb time is also relatively short.)
If you find it difficult to climb the mountain on foot, there are also cable cars and the ‘Namsan Circular Bus’ that you can use depending on the situation.
(The northern path takes a short time to climb, but it has the steepest slope and is physically difficult, so check it out in advance.)

Namsan Tower, which is an essential part of Seoul tourism, is a great place to enjoy the panoramic view of Seoul along with Lotte Tower, and it is also the best course to experience mountain hiking, which is an essential part of Korean tourism, so be sure to visit it.

reviews.text:
It is a nice walking trail that allows you to take a walk around Namsan. The total length is about 7km, which is not long, and allows you to enjoy the nature of Namsan and the cityscape at the same time.

The road is well-maintained, so many people use it for light exercise or as a date course, and there are benches and observation points here and there, making it a great place to take a break and experience the diverse scenery of Seoul depending on the season.
At night, the lighting is soft and creates a romantic atmosphere, providing a unique pleasure to those who climb Namsan Mountain to see the night view of Seoul.

reviews.author: NAMTAEK KIM
reviews.text:
The Namsan Trail circles Namsan starting from N Seoul Tower. This road was originally created as a road for cars.
However, as Namsan becomes a park, it is changing into a path for people to walk rather than cars.

The North Ring Road is called the ‘Well-being Jogging Mecca Road’ and vehicular traffic is completely restricted. Since May 2011, only circular buses can pass through the southern ring road. This is a consideration for those who want to see Namsan on foot.

There are various ways to approach Namsan Trail. Usually, subway bases such as Myeongdong Station, Dongguk University Station, and Seoul Station are widely used.
There are 15 official access roads to Namsan Dullegil. Among these, the most loved places are Myeongdong Station and Dongguk University Station.

Namsan Library is a 15-minute walk up Sopa-gil from Exit 1 of Myeongdong Station.
Namsan Library includes the Seoul Education Research and Information Center, which has an observatory-shaped dome on the roof, and the Ahn Jung-geun Memorial Hall. From here, you can also follow the stairs made of wooden deck to Jamdubong Photo Island and go to N Seoul Tower.

However, the Namsan Trail follows the southern ring road from the entrance to Namsan Park. This road has a sidewalk for pedestrians on the right side of the automobile road.
The asphalt is covered with cushioned urethane, making it comfortable to walk on. It is 1.8km from the entrance to Namsan Park to N Seoul Tower. You have to walk steadily uphill for about 30 minutes.

N Seoul Tower is the summit of Namsan Mountain and the terminal point of the cable car. Enjoy the southern view of Seoul from here.
The tens of thousands of love keys hanging on the deck observatory are also a must-see. We also check the central point of Seoul.
From N Seoul Tower, the trail leads back down to the parking lot. From now on, it is a gently sloping downhill road to the entrance of the National Theater where it meets the North Ring Road.

If you come down from the N Seoul Tower parking lot for about 10 minutes, you will come to a place with an open view.
This place, where the southern photo island is located, has the best view on the Namsan trail. The sight of N Seoul Tower, piercing the sky above the towering Namsan Mountain, is beautiful.
The close-knit houses and alleys in the residential area of ​​Huam-dong at the bottom of the mountain are also cozy. If you look far south, Gwanaksan Mountain across the Han River is so close you can touch it.
(Gilsupseom Island, Sanhwan Kim)

reviews.author: Lets
reviews.text:
Take the free elevator (Namsan Ormi) from Myeongdong Station and go up a little on the other side of the cable car station, and you will see a sign for the Namsan Dullegil / Namsan Tower intersection.

In terms of taking the cable car, there are two ways to climb Namsan Tower: walking up directly or taking a cable car (you can also take bus '01B' and take a big turn... takes about 30 to 40 minutes). If you walk along the Namsan trail for about 45 minutes, you will reach the '01A' bus stop, which takes you up to Namsan Tower in 5 minutes.

reviews.text: Namsan Dulegal is always nice to walk. Coconut milk makes walking easier. The trees are nice, and the autumn leaves fall late in the south. The road coming down from the beacon tower to the old Children's Center had beautiful fall foliage.

reviews.author: BONG
reviews.text:
Now that there are more Chinese people, the square is not as peaceful and quiet as it used to be.
It is a great place to enjoy the night view of Seoul, but it has recently become popular with foreigners, making the area around Namsan Tower very crowded and a place where Chinese is spoken loudly.

In addition to making noise and playing on the streets, people can also be seen shouting, smoking, eating, and throwing away trash, so management is necessary.

reviews.author: pea
reviews.text: Namsan Octagon Square located in Namsan Tower. You can see the octagonal pavilion, the beacon fire tower, and the Namsan Tower observatory. Lovers can wear pretty locks as a promise of love. You can also occasionally see traditional Korean performances at Namsan Octagon Square.

reviews.author: Brightwise PARK
reviews.text: Along with Namsangol Hanok Village, this place offers various folk entertainment events for foreign visitors. On a clear day without fine dust, if you go before sunset, you can enjoy the beautiful scenery of Bukhansan Mountain and downtown Seoul, followed by the night view of downtown Seoul.
